in short intervals and the size of the Chebyshev functions.

unit_result_entry.title: Positive theta increment certifies a prime in the target interval
unit_result_entry.why_material: The source converts the theta-error lemma into prime existence by showing the Chebyshev-function increment over the target multiplicative interval is positive. This is the central semantic bridge from an analytic error estimate to a discrete existence conclusion.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: At this stage the argument applies only for x at least e^35; the remaining lines construct a separate descent to smaller x.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: The implication is prose-supported, but the displayed increment and constant inequality are formula-dependent and should be scan-verified.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Piecewise endpoint certification of a uniform theta-error bound
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The proof combines a psi bound with an explicit psi-theta discrepancy, defines a normalized error expression, and certifies it on exponential intervals using a bound at each left endpoint and evaluation at the right endpoint. A finite table covers the middle range and Theorem 1 covers the tail.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Bootstrapping short-interval coverage downward with maximal prime gaps
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: A certified maximal gap up to a high cutoff yields a lower threshold through a simple inequality; recomputing a smaller maximal gap below that threshold permits repeated descent until exhaustive search is cheap. This is a reusable analytic-to-finite bootstrapping pattern.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: Uniform theta control proves the short-interval statement at large scale, while maximal-gap certificates repeatedly lower the boundary until exhaustive verification becomes feasible.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The source reports rather than reproduces the external gap certificate and final computations.
